glosses: to creak, to crunch, to scrunch (to emit a crunching or creaking sound)
wydawać swoisty dźwięk, jaki powstaje przy tarciu niegładkich i suchych powierzchni
The sound produced by anything that creaks; a creaking.
To make a prolonged sharp grating or squeaking sound, as by the friction of hard substances.

examples.text: Then when the four ropes were arranged the coffin was placed upon them. He watched it descend; it seemed descending for ever. At last a thud was heard; the ropes creaked as they were drawn up.
He heard the creaking of the bolt as it came slowly back, and at the same moment he found the monkey's paw, and frantically breathed his third and last wish.

glosses: To produce a creaking sound with.

examples.text: Creaking my shoes on the plain masonry.

I miss the polished brass, the powerful black horses,
The drivers creaking the seats of the baroque hearses, […]

glosses: To suffer from strain or old age.

examples.text: Fascinating though this high-minded re-reading was, certain crucial joints of the play creaked a good deal under the strain.
The whole basis of feudalism, especially in the more intensively farmed champion arable landscapes of the Midlands, was starting to creak.

glosses: To crush something, especially food, with a noisy crackling sound.

examples.text: When I came home, Susan was watching TV with her feet up on the couch, crunching a piece of celery.
And their white tusks crunch'd o'er the whiter skull,

glosses: To be crushed with a noisy crackling sound.

examples.text: Beetles crunched beneath the men's heavy boots as they worked.

glosses: To calculate or otherwise process (e.g. to crunch numbers: to perform mathematical calculations). Presumably from the sound made by mechanical calculators.

examples.text: That metadata makes it much easier for the search engine to crunch the data for queries.

glosses: To grind or press with violence and noise.

examples.text: The sound of our vessel crunching her way through the new ice is not easy to be described.

The departure was not unduly prolonged.[…]Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments on the subject of Divine Intention in the disposition of buckets; farewells and last commiserations; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.

glosses: To emit a grinding or crunching noise.

examples.text: There were sounds in the air above his head – sounds of the crunching and rattling of the loose, smooth stones as his neighbors moved about[…]

glosses: To cause the gears to emit a crunching sound by releasing the clutch before the gears are properly synchronised.
To compress (data) using a particular algorithm, so that it can be restored by decrunching.

examples.text: PackIt will not crunch executables, unless told to do so.

glosses: To make employees work overtime in order to meet a deadline in the development of a project.
A noisy crackling sound; the sound usually associated with crunching.
A critical moment or event.

examples.text: It always pains me (slightly) when a flaming young radical like Neil Miller turns out when the crunch comes to be such an ardent defender of the status quo.

The friends, on the contrary, argue that Job does not "know", that only God knows; yet, when it comes to the crunch, they themselves seem to know as much as God knows: for example, that Job is a guilty sinner.

glosses: A problem that leads to a crisis.

examples.text: The crunch is characterized by extremely depressed liquidity and deteriorated balance sheet positions for households, corporations, and financial institutions[…]

glosses: A form of abdominal exercise, based on a sit-up but in which the lower back remains in contact with the floor.

examples.text: But even I draw the line at “doing crunches” in designer clothes. Fashion sneakers are for swanking around the shops, not for running in. And so, like everyone else, I wear grotty old tracksuits earmarked for Oxfam, and tragic free festival T-shirts that give away my age.

glosses: The overtime work required to catch up and finish a project, usually in the final weeks of development before release.
A dessert consisting of a crunchy topping with fruit underneath.
The symbol #.
A small piece created by crushing; a piece of material with a friable or crunchy texture.

examples.text: Smear the peanut butter, fluff, and a bit of the nutella all over, even to the very edge of the wrap. Sprinkle the crunches on top and then start rolling from one of the non-trimmed edges

glosses: A shortage.

examples.text: But a supply crunch, which is already affecting the drive, could slow it down further.

glosses: Moderate distortion.

A card game similar to group solitaire.

examples.text: "I had the very devil of a squeak for it," he went on. "I did the hurdles over two or three garden-walls, but so did the flyer who was on my tracks, and he drove me back into the straight and down to High Street like any lamplighter. […]

glosses: To emit a short, high-pitched sound.

examples.text: But I must warn you that chipboard floors are always likely to squeak. The material is still being used in new-builds, but developers now use adhesive to bed and joint it, rather than screws or nails. I suspect the adhesive will eventually embrittle and crack, resulting in the same squeaking problems as before.

glosses: To inform, to squeal.

examples.text: If he be obstinate, put a civil question to him upon the rack, and he squeaks, I warrant him.

glosses: To speak or sound in a high-pitched manner.

To win or progress by a narrow margin.

examples.text: […] allowing Parkinson to squeak into the final by a half-point margin.

France were transformed from the feeble, divided unit that had squeaked past Wales in the semi-final, their half-backs finding the corners with beautifully judged kicks from hand, the forwards making yards with every drive and a reorganised Kiwi line-out beginning to malfunction.

glosses: Produire un bruit aigre, strident et métallique.

examples.text: Ses deux garçons étaient tisserands, et dans ce vieux nid on entendait grincer les métiers et siffler les navettes du matin au soir.

glosses: Produire un bruit aigre en serrant les dents les unes contre les autres sous l’action de l’agacement, de la douleur ou de la colère.

examples.text: Grincer des dents ; (Plus rare) Grincer les dents.
Le bruit de la scie fait grincer les dents.

Du fond de ses yeux creux flambent des feux ardents.
D’un orteil convulsif, comme un lion sauvage,
Il fouille la poussière et fait grincer ses dents.
– Tonnerre… grinça-t-il, le papier n’y est pas… Tu m’as roulé.

[…] son grand livre De la Raison chez les Grecs. Il y travaille depuis trois ans ; toujours en ayant l’air de grincer des dents ; il tord les arguments comme du linge, il veut raisonner serré, lui, il ne veut pas d’une logique lâche, — ce qui le constipe, il paraît, et lui donne de grands maux de tête.

glosses: Crier, en parlant particulièrement de la chauve-souris.

examples.text: — Vraiment, tu es d’une amabilité au-dessus de tout éloge, ce soir ! grinça-t-elle.

examples.text: Al apuntar la noche se encendió el alumbrado de gas, y á los ejercicios de los Alcides sustituyó una plaga de farsantes; los unos cantando al armónico son de un organillo portátil; los otros entonando malas trobas acompañadas de un chirriante violín.

¡Je! ¡Je! —continuaba, siempre hablando para sí y siempre riéndose mientras la lima chirriaba cada vez con más fuerza, mordiendo el metal con sus dientes de acero—. ¡Je! ¡Je! Pobre Daniel, dirán los míos, ya chochea.

glosses: Producir un sonido por efecto del calor intenso, como el de la grasa al fuego.

examples.text: Yo, por no alcanzar algo de barato de aquel repartimiento, y por que no me cogiera en mentira y parecerme cosa fácil levantar un bigote, sabiendo levantar dos mil embustes y testimonios, sin quitarme el ferreruelo ni dar muestras de turbación, saqué un hierro de los que estaban al fuego, que se había estado escaldando desde el principio del rebato y escaramuza; y, por no tener en qué probarlo y parecer diligente, tomé un peine, encajéselo en aquella selva de clines, arriméle el hierro, y levantándose una humareda horrenda, al son de un sonoroso chirriar y de un olor de pie puerco chamuscado, le hice chicharrón todo el pelamen.

La gente que venía del puente podía ver las filas de teas ardiendo que fileteaba los portales; y allí, el alegre y bullicioso hablar de las negras y negros, el chirriar de la grasa hirviendo que preparaban para las frituras, la afluencia de los compradores, y la diversidad de las castas, pues mezcladas andaban el altivo castellano con el cargado y francote catalán; el tosco gallego con el insolente y afeminado zambo, el ardiente negro con el indio humillado.
